page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c5.6xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the KVM hypervisor. The instance is powered by a dedicated 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8163 processor providing 24 virtual CPUs derived from 12 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It includes 48.0 GB of total RAM, maintaining a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core. Cache configuration includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 35 MB shared L3 cache, with instruction set support for AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI alongside AES acceleration. Networking capabilities provide an 8 Gbps baseline bandwidth. The instance features no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached cloud disks, and does not include hardware GPU acceleration or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark measurements indicate consistent mid-tier multi-threaded compute capabilities alongside limited single-core execution speed. Single-core performance falls within lower percentiles, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 991.0 and a stress-ng single-core rating of 1106.0. Single-threaded data handling tests also show constraints, such as 19.25 GB/sec in gzip compression. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics perform within the middle tier, producing a stress-ng multi-core score of 17696.41 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 7736.0. Memory bandwidth delivers 96.87 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 52.35 GB/sec for uncached writes, while caching enables small-block reads up to 986.81 GB/sec.

Application and domain-specific tests demonstrate steady average throughput under parallel execution. The instance reached 16.98 million operations per second during Redis SET testing, a static web serving throughput of 13.48 GB/sec, and a software compilation score of 14250.0 in Clang. CPU-based small LLM inference achieves 1157.03 prompt tokens per second and 77.76 generation tokens per second on a 135M model, though larger models exhibit slower prompt processing (29.1 tokens per second on a 7B model).

In terms of qualitative efficiency, the ecs.c5.6xlarge offers a balanced resource density tailored for scale-out parallel workloads rather than low-latency single-thread tasks. The strict 2 GB per core ratio makes it unsuitable for large in-memory caches, but well matched for distributed web serving tiers, parallel CI/CD compilation, and mid-sized batch processing pipelines that require predictable multi-threaded CPU allocation.
